ref: Feigenbaum Teen Siddur, Nusach Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharis, Hashkamas Ha'boker, Elokai Neshama
he: אֱלֹהַי נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַֽתָּ בִּי טְהוֹרָה הִיא אַתָּה בְרָאתָהּ אַתָּה יְצַרְתָּהּ אַתָּה נְפַחְתָּהּ בִּי וְאַתָּה מְשַׁמְּ֒רָהּ בְּקִרְבִּי וְאַתָּה עָתִיד לִטְּ֒לָהּ מִמֶּֽנִּי וּלְהַחֲזִירָהּ בִּי לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַנְּ֒שָׁמָה בְקִרְבִּי מוֹדֶה אֲנִי לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהַי וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתַי רִבּוֹן כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים אֲדוֹן כָּל הַנְּ֒שָׁמוֹת: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה הַמַּחֲזִיר נְשָׁמוֹת לִפְגָרִים מֵתִים:

textBlocks.text: Hashem Who takes care of me the neshamah that You personally placed in me is a pure neshamah! You formed it (uniquely for me); You breathed it into me, You make sure it stays in me (and keeps me alive); and I know that eventually You will take it back. (Therefore, I must take advantage of it while I can!) And I believe that You will return it to me

at Techiyas Hameisim. As long as my neshamah is in me, I thank You, Hashem, Who takes care of me and Bnei Yisrael throughout our history; You are the Master of all that happens and of all souls. You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; Who restores the neshamahs to dead bodies.
OK I have a body and a soul. What can I do to ensure they work together successfully?
